body:
Markets extended their brutal selloff today as the total crypto market cap shed another 3.00% to $2.4 trillion, marking 7 straight days of declines that have wiped over $300 billion in value since the peak. The fear and greed index plunged to 11, hitting extreme fear territory as traders capitulated across the board. Volume surged to $165.2 billion as panic selling accelerated, with liquidations reportedly hitting $1.8 billion as overleveraged positions got crushed. The broader risk-off sentiment has crypto looking increasingly correlated with traditional markets, and the technical damage is becoming severe.

Bitcoin closed at $67,007, down 3.56% on the day and now sitting 11.59% lower for the week after briefly touching $65,000 overnight. The selloff triggered a cascade of stop losses and forced liquidations around the $66,000 level, which had been defended multiple times over the past month. BTC is now testing critical support at $65,000-67,000, with the next major floor at $60,000. The 50-day moving average at $69,200 has turned into resistance, and momentum indicators are flashing maximum fear signals. If $65,000 breaks decisively, we could see a violent move toward $58,000-60,000 where the 200-day moving average sits.

Ethereum got hammered even harder, dropping 5.23% to $1,874 as the ETH/BTC ratio continues its relentless decline toward multi-month lows. Solana fell 5.04% to $75, while BNB led the losers with a 6.04% plunge to $637. Interestingly, XRP showed relative strength with only a 2.02% decline to $1.23, and Uniswap actually posted a small gain of 0.14% to $2.90, suggesting some rotation into perceived value plays. The altcoin rout has been indiscriminate though, with most major tokens down 8-12% for the week as Bitcoin dominance climbed back above 55.9%.

The macro backdrop is turning increasingly hostile as geopolitical tensions escalate with new US strikes on Iran, prompting fresh Treasury sanctions targeting 4 crypto exchanges. Meanwhile, regulatory uncertainty persists despite positive developments like Stripe, Visa, and Mastercard backing a new stablecoin platform. The Fed remains in blackout mode ahead of next week's meeting, but bond yields have been creeping higher, putting pressure on risk assets. Crypto PACs scored another bipartisan victory in June primaries, but that political tailwind is being overwhelmed by immediate risk-off flows.

The next 48 hours are critical as Bitcoin tests the $65,000-67,000 support zone with weakening momentum and deteriorating market structure. A break below $65,000 would likely trigger another wave of algorithmic selling and could send BTC toward $60,000 quickly. On the upside, any relief rally needs to reclaim $70,000 to change the near-term bearish narrative. Watch for Fed commentary, any escalation in Middle East tensions, and whether institutional flows show up as a backstop at these levels. The technical damage suggests this correction has further to run unless we see a decisive reversal above key resistance levels.
